questions.question: A system which has both mass and energy transfer across the boundary is called a(n):
questions.answer: Open systems exchange both matter and energy with the surroundings.

questions.question: Which graph represents the relationship between $K_{eq}$ and temperature for an exothermic reaction?
questions.answer: Raising temperature shifts an exothermic reaction towards reactants, so $K_{eq}$ decreases.

questions.question: The solubility of $\mathrm{Mn(IO_3)_2}$ is $4.8\times10^{-3}$ M. What is the value of $K_{sp}$?
When comparing 1.0 M solutions of bases, the base with the lowest $[OH^-]$ is the:
questions.answer: A weaker base ionises less, giving less $OH^-$ and a smaller $K_b$.
options: weakest base and it has the largest $K_b$ value.
strongest base and it has the largest $K_b$ value.
weakest base and it has the smallest $K_b$ value.
strongest base and it has the smallest $K_b$ value.

questions.question:
Consider the following solubility data at 25 °C.

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline \text{Compound} & K_{sp}\\\hline \mathrm{CuSO_4} & 2.28\times10^{-2}\\ \mathrm{BaSO_4} & 1.08\times10^{-10}\\ \mathrm{CaSO_4} & 4.93\times10^{-5}\\\hline\end{array}$$

What is the order of cation concentration in the saturated solutions, from highest to lowest?
questions.answer: All are 1:1 salts, so cation concentration $=\sqrt{K_{sp}}$: the larger $K_{sp}$, the higher the concentration.

questions.question: What is the advantage of a biofuel compared with a fuel derived from fossil fuels?
questions.answer: Biofuels come from biomass that regrows quickly, so they are renewable.
options: No energy is used to extract and isolate a biofuel from its source.
The amount of energy per mole is greater for the biofuel compound.
Only the biofuel is produced naturally in an endothermic reaction.
The biofuel can be replenished quickly using natural processes.

questions.question: A sample of compound M is analysed in a mass spectrometer where it forms the molecular ion $M^+$: $M + e^- \rightarrow M^+ + 2e^-$. Some molecular ions fragment as $M^+\rightarrow X^+ + Y$ and $M^+\rightarrow X + Y^+$. The mass spectrum would show peaks due to which species?
questions.answer: Only charged species are deflected and detected.

questions.question:
Pure water self-ionises: $\mathrm{2H_2O(l) \rightleftharpoons H_3O^+(aq) + OH^-(aq)}$. The ionisation constant at constant pressure is:

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline T\ (^\circ\text{C}) & 0&25&50&75&100\\\hline K_w & 1.1\times10^{-15}&1.0\times10^{-14}&5.5\times10^{-14}&2.0\times10^{-13}&5.6\times10^{-13}\\\hline\end{array}$$

Which statement about pure water is correct?
questions.answer: $K_w$ rises with temperature and $[H_3O^+]=\sqrt{K_w}$, so it increases (and pH falls).
options: Its pH will increase with increasing temperature.
Its pH will always be exactly 7 at any temperature.

questions.question: Which best describes the properties of compounds X and Y shown?
questions.answer: X contains carboxylic acid groups; Y is an amine.
options: X is basic and Y is acidic.
X is acidic and Y is basic.

questions.question: Hydrogen is produced from methane: $\mathrm{2H_2O(g) + CH_4(g) \rightleftharpoons CO_2(g) + 4H_2(g)}$. The expression for the equilibrium constant for the reverse reaction is:
questions.answer: For the reverse reaction the expression is inverted.

questions.question: For $\mathrm{2H_2O(g) + CH_4(g) \rightleftharpoons CO_2(g) + 4H_2(g)}$ at equilibrium, if the temperature is constant and the volume is halved, the immediate concentration of hydrogen will:
questions.answer: Halving the volume immediately doubles every concentration (before any shift).

questions.question: Infrared spectroscopy detects frequencies of infrared light absorbed by a molecule. These absorptions are based on:
questions.answer: IR energy excites bond vibrations.
options: movement of electrons between molecular energy levels.
movement of electrons between different atomic energy levels.
bending or stretching of covalent bonds in molecules.
absorption of radiation by nuclei placed in a magnetic field.

questions.question: Carbon tetrachloride, $\mathrm{CCl_4}$, is often used as a solvent. Which statement about it is FALSE?
questions.answer: Methane reacts with chlorine by substitution, not addition.
options: Its main intermolecular forces are dispersion forces.
It is the product of an addition reaction between methane and chlorine in the presence of UV light.

questions.question:
Which indicator is most suitable for the titration of ammonia with hydrochloric acid?

$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline \text{Indicator (pH)} & 0\text{–}4&5\text{–}6&7&8\text{–}10&11\text{–}14\\\hline \text{Litmus}&\text{red}&\text{red}&\text{purple}&\text{blue}&\text{blue}\\ \text{Methyl orange}&\text{red/orange}&\text{yellow}&\text{yellow}&\text{yellow}&\text{yellow}\\ \text{Phenolphthalein}&\text{colourless}&\text{colourless}&\text{colourless}&\text{pink/red}&\text{red}\\\hline\end{array}$$
questions.answer: A weak base–strong acid titration has an acidic equivalence point, within methyl orange's colour change.
options: All three would be equally suitable

questions.question: What is the relationship between the two molecules shown?
questions.answer: Butan-2-ol is $\mathrm{C_4H_{10}O}$ and butan-2-one is $\mathrm{C_4H_8O}$; different molecular formulae, so they are not isomers.

questions.question: Which combination could be used to prepare a buffer solution?
questions.answer: A buffer needs a weak acid and its conjugate base.

questions.question: Which statement about 10.0 mL of 0.10 M HCl and 10.0 mL of 0.10 M $\mathrm{CH_3COOH}$ solutions is true?
questions.answer: Both contain 0.0010 mol of monoprotic acid, so each neutralises the same amount of base.
options: Each solution will have the same electrical conductivity.
Each solution will react completely with 10.0 mL of 0.10 M NaOH solution.
Each solution will react at the same rate with 1.00 g of magnesium ribbon.
The concentration of $H_3O^+$ will be greater in the $\mathrm{CH_3COOH}$ solution.

questions.question: 100 mL of water was heated by burning methanol in a spirit burner. What is the maximum temperature change of the water when 0.500 g of methanol is completely combusted? Assume all heat is absorbed by the water. $\Delta H_c$(methanol) $=-726$ kJ/mol.
Aspartame is an artificial sweetener with the structure shown. What are the functional groups labelled I, II, III and IV respectively?
questions.answer: I is COOH, II is $NH_2$, III is CONH, IV is COOR.

questions.question: How would the concentration of $Pb^{2+}$(aq) in equilibrium with $PbI_2$(s) be affected if the concentration of $I^-$(aq) were doubled?
questions.answer: $K_{sp}=[Pb^{2+}][I^-]^2$ is constant, so doubling $[I^-]$ divides $[Pb^{2+}]$ by 4.

questions.question: A student takes a 50.0 mL sample from a saturated solution of silver chloride kept at 25 °C. Write an equilibrium equation for solid silver chloride and its ions in solution.
questions.answer: $\mathrm{AgCl(s) \rightleftharpoons Ag^+(aq) + Cl^-(aq)}$

questions.question: A student takes a 50.0 mL sample from a saturated solution of silver chloride kept at 25 °C. Calculate the mass of silver ions in the 50.0 mL sample.
Sodium hydrogen carbonate ($\mathrm{NaHCO_3}$) is amphiprotic. Write TWO net ionic equations showing its amphiprotic behaviour.
questions.answer:
As a base: $\mathrm{HCO_3^-(aq) + H_3O^+(aq) \rightarrow H_2CO_3(aq) + H_2O(l)}$

As an acid: $\mathrm{HCO_3^-(aq) + OH^-(aq) \rightarrow CO_3^{2-}(aq) + H_2O(l)}$

questions.question: Sodium hydrogen carbonate is amphiprotic: $\mathrm{HCO_3^- + H_3O^+ \rightarrow H_2CO_3 + H_2O}$ and $\mathrm{HCO_3^- + OH^- \rightarrow CO_3^{2-} + H_2O}$. Identify ONE conjugate acid–base pair from these equations.
questions.answer: $H_2CO_3/HCO_3^-$ (also acceptable: $HCO_3^-/CO_3^{2-}$, $H_3O^+/H_2O$, $H_2O/OH^-$).

questions.question: Hydrofluoric acid is a weak acid. The pH of a 0.025 M solution of hydrofluoric acid is 2.39. Calculate the $K_a$ of hydrofluoric acid.
Hydrofluoric acid is a weak acid. The pH of a 0.025 M solution of hydrofluoric acid is 2.39. Given $K_a=7.93\times10^{-4}$, calculate the p$K_a$.
Hydrofluoric acid is a weak acid. The pH of a 0.025 M solution of hydrofluoric acid is 2.39. Calculate the percentage dissociation of the acid.

The reaction $\mathrm{A_2(g) + 2B_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2AB_2(g)}$ takes place in a 2.00 L closed flask at 25 °C. The graph shows the number of moles of each gas over the first 10 minutes. Using data from the graph, determine the value of $K_{eq}$.

The reaction $\mathrm{A_2(g) + 2B_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2AB_2(g)}$ takes place in a 2.00 L closed flask at 25 °C. The graph shows the number of moles of each gas over the first 10 minutes. ($K_{eq}=0.444$.) At 15 minutes some $B_2$ was removed. At 20 minutes the flask contained $[A_2]=1.05$, $[B_2]=0.40$ and $[AB_2]=0.30$ mol L⁻¹. Determine whether the system has reached equilibrium at 20 minutes and describe the rates of the forward and reverse reactions at this time.
questions.answer:
$$Q=\frac{0.30^2}{1.05\times0.40^2}=0.536$$

$Q>K_{eq}$, so the system is not at equilibrium. It is still shifting left: the rate of the reverse reaction is greater than the rate of the forward reaction.

questions.question: Consider $\mathrm{2NO(g) + O_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NO_2(g)}$, $\Delta H=-556$ kJ. The temperature is increased at time $t$. State the effect on the equilibrium position and complete the graph to show how the concentrations of reactants and product are affected.
questions.answer: The forward reaction is exothermic, so the equilibrium shifts left. From $t$, [NO] and $[O_2]$ rise and $[NO_2]$ falls gradually (no instantaneous jump) in the ratio 2 : 1 : 2, then level off at new constant values.

questions.question:
A manufacturer claims its pain-relieving tablets contain 100% aspirin. A back titration was used.

**Step 1:** Three tablets, each 300.0 mg, were crushed and dissolved in exactly 100.0 mL of 0.204 mol L⁻¹ NaOH (excess). The mixture was boiled to ensure complete reaction.

**Step 2:** 20.0 mL portions of the solution from step 1 were titrated with 0.125 mol L⁻¹ HCl using phenolphthalein; the average titre was 17.89 mL.

Calculate the number of moles of NaOH added in step 1.

A manufacturer claims its pain-relieving tablets contain 100% aspirin. A back titration was used.

**Step 1:** Three tablets, each 300.0 mg, were crushed and dissolved in exactly 100.0 mL of 0.204 mol L⁻¹ NaOH (excess). The mixture was boiled to ensure complete reaction.

**Step 2:** 20.0 mL portions of the solution from step 1 were titrated with 0.125 mol L⁻¹ HCl using phenolphthalein; the average titre was 17.89 mL.

Calculate how many moles of NaOH reacted with the aspirin.
questions.answer:
$n(HCl)=0.125\times0.01789=2.236\times10^{-3}$ mol $=n(NaOH)$ in 20.0 mL

Excess NaOH in 100.0 mL $=5\times2.236\times10^{-3}=0.011181$ mol

NaOH reacted $=0.0204-0.011181=9.22\times10^{-3}$ mol

questions.question:
A manufacturer claims its pain-relieving tablets contain 100% aspirin. A back titration was used.

**Step 1:** Three tablets, each 300.0 mg, were crushed and dissolved in exactly 100.0 mL of 0.204 mol L⁻¹ NaOH (excess). The mixture was boiled to ensure complete reaction.

**Step 2:** 20.0 mL portions of the solution from step 1 were titrated with 0.125 mol L⁻¹ HCl using phenolphthalein; the average titre was 17.89 mL.

($9.22\times10^{-3}$ mol of NaOH reacted with the aspirin.) Each aspirin molecule requires two hydroxide ions for complete reaction. Calculate the percentage by mass of aspirin in one tablet. ($M$ = 180.154 g mol⁻¹)
questions.answer:
$n(\text{aspirin})=\dfrac{9.22\times10^{-3}}{2}=4.61\times10^{-3}$ mol

Mass in 3 tablets $=4.61\times10^{-3}\times180.154=0.830$ g, i.e. 276.8 mg per tablet

$\%=\dfrac{276.8}{300.0}\times100=92.3\%$

questions.question: Dacron is a polyester used in clothes and water bottles. Part of its structure is shown. Give the structural formulae of the two monomers that react to form it.
questions.answer:
Benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic (terephthalic) acid: $\mathrm{HOOC{-}C_6H_4{-}COOH}$ (COOH groups on opposite carbons of the ring)

Ethane-1,2-diol: $\mathrm{HO{-}CH_2CH_2{-}OH}$

questions.question: Dacron is a polyester used in clothes and water bottles. Part of its structure is shown. Name the other product of this polymerisation reaction.
questions.answer: Water (condensation polymerisation).

questions.question: Dacron is a polyester used in clothes and water bottles. Part of its structure is shown. Predict the effect on the polyester's rigidity and melting point as the polymer chains increase in length. Explain your predictions.
questions.answer: Both increase. Longer chains have more points of contact, so the total dipole–dipole forces (between polar ester groups) and dispersion forces between chains are greater. More energy is needed to separate the chains (higher melting point). Chains also move and slide past each other less easily, helped by the stiff benzene rings and increased entanglement, so the material is more rigid.

questions.question: The structure of addition polymers can be modelled using Molymods. Outline an advantage and a disadvantage of using models in science.
questions.answer:
Advantage: a model lets us visualise something too small to see, such as the 3D arrangement of atoms and bonds in a polymer chain.

Disadvantage: it is a simplification and can mislead, e.g. it shows only a short chain and not intermolecular forces, relative bond lengths exactly or molecular motion.

questions.answer:

questions.question: The flowchart shows the synthesis of some organic compounds. Give the full structural formulae of compounds E and F.
questions.answer:
E, N-methylpropanamide: $\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH_2{-}C({=}O){-}NH{-}CH_3}$

questions.question: The flowchart shows the synthesis of some organic compounds. Identify processes Y and Z. Give TWO experimental conditions required for each.
questions.answer:
**Y: esterification.** Concentrated $H_2SO_4$ catalyst; heating under reflux.

**Z: fermentation.** Yeast (enzyme catalyst); anaerobic conditions in aqueous solution at about 25–37 °C.

questions.question: Compare the uses, structure and properties of soaps and anionic synthetic detergents. Include a diagram in your answer.
questions.answer:
**Structure:** both are long non-polar hydrocarbon tails with a charged polar head.

- Soap: $\mathrm{CH_3(CH_2)_{16}{-}COO^-\,Na^+}$ (carboxylate head; made by saponification of fats and oils)
- Anionic detergent: $\mathrm{CH_3(CH_2)_{11}{-}C_6H_4{-}SO_3^-\,Na^+}$ (sulfonate head; made mainly from petrochemicals)

Diagram description: a micelle with the tails buried in an oil droplet and the negative heads on the surface facing water.

**Properties:** both act as surfactants and emulsify grease as micelles. Soap forms an insoluble scum with $Ca^{2+}$/$Mg^{2+}$ in hard water and is protonated in acidic water; detergents work well in both. Soap is readily biodegradable; detergents are biodegradable only if their chains are largely unbranched.

**Uses:** soaps for personal washing; anionic detergents for laundry powders and dishwashing liquids.

questions.question: Hex-1-ene gas burns in oxygen: $\mathrm{C_6H_{12}(g) + 9O_2(g) \rightarrow 6CO_2(g) + 6H_2O(g)}$ (25 °C, 100 kPa). The enthalpy change is $-3773$ kJ/mol. State whether this favours a spontaneous reaction and justify.
questions.answer: Yes. $\Delta H$ is negative (exothermic), which lowers the enthalpy of the system and makes $\Delta G=\Delta H-T\Delta S$ more negative.

questions.question: Hex-1-ene gas burns in oxygen: $\mathrm{C_6H_{12}(g) + 9O_2(g) \rightarrow 6CO_2(g) + 6H_2O(g)}$ (25 °C, 100 kPa). The entropy change is 188 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. State whether this favours a spontaneous reaction and justify.
questions.answer: Yes. $\Delta S$ is positive: 10 mol of gas become 12 mol, increasing disorder, and the $-T\Delta S$ term makes $\Delta G$ more negative.

questions.question: Hex-1-ene gas burns in oxygen: $\mathrm{C_6H_{12}(g) + 9O_2(g) \rightarrow 6CO_2(g) + 6H_2O(g)}$ (25 °C, 100 kPa). Given $\Delta H=-3773$ kJ/mol and $\Delta S=188$ J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, determine with a calculation whether the reaction is spontaneous at 25 °C.
questions.answer:
$$\Delta G=\Delta H-T\Delta S=-3773-298.15\times0.188=-3829\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

$\Delta G<0$, so the reaction is spontaneous at 25 °C.

questions.question: Most plants contain pH-sensitive pigments. Outline a method for preparing a natural indicator.
questions.answer: Chop a few red cabbage leaves into small pieces, cover with water in a beaker and boil gently for about 10 minutes. Cool, then filter (or decant) and keep the purple filtrate as the indicator.

questions.question: Explain why a natural indicator solution can be used to qualitatively determine the acidity or basicity of a solution. Include a suitable equation.
questions.answer:
The pigment is a weak acid whose conjugate base has a different colour:

$\mathrm{HIn(aq) + H_2O(l) \rightleftharpoons H_3O^+(aq) + In^-(aq)}$

In acid, added $H_3O^+$ shifts the equilibrium left, showing the colour of HIn. In base, $OH^-$ removes $H_3O^+$, shifting it right to show the colour of $In^-$. Comparing with known acids and bases indicates whether a solution is acidic or basic.

questions.question:
Hydrogen sulfide in solution is a diprotic acid:

$\mathrm{H_2S + H_2O \rightleftharpoons HS^- + H_3O^+}$, $K_{a1}=9.6\times10^{-8}$

$\mathrm{HS^- + H_2O \rightleftharpoons S^{2-} + H_3O^+}$, $K_{a2}=1.3\times10^{-14}$

A student estimating the pH of 0.010 M $H_2S$ assumed (1) only the first ionisation need be considered and (2) the equilibrium concentration of $H_2S$ is about 0.010 M.

Explain why these two assumptions are justified.
questions.answer:
1. $K_{a2}$ is about $10^6$–$10^7$ times smaller than $K_{a1}$, so the second ionisation contributes a negligible amount of $H_3O^+$.
2. $K_{a1}$ is very small, so only a tiny fraction of $H_2S$ ionises (about 0.3%), leaving its concentration essentially 0.010 M.

questions.question:
Hydrogen sulfide in solution is a diprotic acid:

$\mathrm{H_2S + H_2O \rightleftharpoons HS^- + H_3O^+}$, $K_{a1}=9.6\times10^{-8}$

$\mathrm{HS^- + H_2O \rightleftharpoons S^{2-} + H_3O^+}$, $K_{a2}=1.3\times10^{-14}$

A student estimating the pH of 0.010 M $H_2S$ assumed (1) only the first ionisation need be considered and (2) the equilibrium concentration of $H_2S$ is about 0.010 M.

Use these assumptions to calculate the pH of the 0.010 M solution.

Boiling points of straight-chain alkanes, primary amines and carboxylic acids of similar molar mass:

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline \multicolumn{2}{|c|}{\text{Alkane}}&\multicolumn{2}{c|}{\text{Amine}}&\multicolumn{2}{c|}{\text{Carboxylic acid}}\\\hline M&\text{BP (°C)}&M&\text{BP (°C)}&M&\text{BP (°C)}\\\hline 58&-1&59&49&61&118\\72&36&73&78&74&141\\86&69&87&104&88&164\\100&98&102&132&102&186\\114&126&115&155&116&205\\\hline\end{array}$$

($M$ in g/mol)

Plot boiling point against molar mass for each homologous series and draw a line of best fit for each.
questions.answer: Plot molar mass on the x-axis and boiling point on the y-axis with labelled units and even scales, use a different symbol for each series with a key, and draw a smooth line of best fit through each set.

questions.question:
Boiling points of straight-chain alkanes, primary amines and carboxylic acids of similar molar mass:

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline \multicolumn{2}{|c|}{\text{Alkane}}&\multicolumn{2}{c|}{\text{Amine}}&\multicolumn{2}{c|}{\text{Carboxylic acid}}\\\hline M&\text{BP (°C)}&M&\text{BP (°C)}&M&\text{BP (°C)}\\\hline 58&-1&59&49&61&118\\72&36&73&78&74&141\\86&69&87&104&88&164\\100&98&102&132&102&186\\114&126&115&155&116&205\\\hline\end{array}$$

($M$ in g/mol)

Identify and explain the trends evident across all three homologous series when boiling point is graphed against molar mass.
questions.answer:
- Within each series, boiling point rises with molar mass: larger molecules have more electrons and surface area, so stronger dispersion forces.
- At similar molar mass: alkanes < primary amines < carboxylic acids. Alkanes are non-polar (dispersion only); amines also form N–H···N hydrogen bonds; carboxylic acids have a polar C=O and O–H, forming two hydrogen bonds between pairs of molecules (dimers), the strongest attraction.
- The gaps between the series narrow as chains lengthen, because dispersion forces from the chain become a larger share of the total.

questions.question: 500.0 mL of 0.12 M NaOH is mixed with 500.0 mL of 0.10 M $\mathrm{Mg(NO_3)_2}$. Write a balanced chemical equation for the reaction.
questions.answer: $\mathrm{2NaOH(aq) + Mg(NO_3)_2(aq) \rightarrow Mg(OH)_2(s) + 2NaNO_3(aq)}$

questions.question: 500.0 mL of 0.12 M NaOH is mixed with 500.0 mL of 0.10 M $\mathrm{Mg(NO_3)_2}$. Determine whether a precipitate will form, supporting your answer with relevant equations.
questions.answer:
$\mathrm{Mg(OH)_2(s) \rightleftharpoons Mg^{2+}(aq) + 2OH^-(aq)}$, $K_{sp}=5.61\times10^{-12}$

After mixing (1.000 L): $[Mg^{2+}]=0.050$ M, $[OH^-]=0.060$ M

$Q=[Mg^{2+}][OH^-]^2=0.050\times0.060^2=1.8\times10^{-4}$

$Q>K_{sp}$, so $\mathrm{Mg(OH)_2}$ precipitates.

questions.question: The IR spectrum and mass spectrum shown are of the same unknown organic compound. What functional group is indicated by the absorption between 3200 and 3500 cm⁻¹?
questions.answer: A hydroxyl (O–H) group of an alcohol (broad band).

questions.question: The IR spectrum and mass spectrum shown are of the same unknown organic compound. From the IR spectrum, how can we be sure the compound is not a ketone or aldehyde?
questions.answer: There is no strong C=O absorption at about 1680–1750 cm⁻¹.

questions.question: The IR spectrum and mass spectrum shown are of the same unknown organic compound. Identify the relative molecular mass of the compound.
questions.answer: 60 (molecular ion at $m/z=60$).

questions.question: The IR spectrum and mass spectrum shown are of the same unknown organic compound. Using the functional group from the IR spectrum and the relative molecular mass, identify the compound and explain your reasoning.
questions.answer:
The IR spectrum shows an alcohol (broad O–H, no C=O, and not the very broad acid O–H). An alcohol with $M_r=60$ is $\mathrm{C_3H_8O}$: propan-1-ol or propan-2-ol.

The base peak at $m/z=31$ is $\mathrm{CH_2OH^+}$ (loss of $C_2H_5$), characteristic of a primary alcohol. Propan-2-ol would instead show a dominant peak at $m/z=45$ ($\mathrm{CH_3CHOH^+}$), which is absent.

The compound is **propan-1-ol**.
